title: Andrew and Tristan Tate: Judge weighs whether to grant bail after hourslong US hearing. Here are the takeaways | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

A US federal judge in Miami is weighing whether to grant bail to controversial online influencersAndrew and Tristan Tateas they fight extradition to the United Kingdom, where they face rape and human trafficking charges. The brothers have repeatedly denied all wrongdoing.

After hours of argument that at times grew tense, a hearing Thursday ended without a ruling from Magistrate Judge Lauren Louis, and the Tates were returned to jail.

The marathon hearing marked the first time the brothers had been seen in public since July, after nearly six weeks held in separate cells at theFederal Detention Centerin Miami.

The Tates entered the courtroom in shackles and matching tan jail jumpsuits, surrounded by four US marshals. Both appeared disheveled, with longer hair and grown-out beards. Tristan winked at a friend seated in the courtroom gallery, who nodded back.

They both took the stand to testify on their own behalf – a move their attorney Joseph McBride described as “highly unusual.”

“I want to fight the case against me and I can’t do it being here,” Tristan Tate told the court. “I can’t speak to my Romanian lawyer. I need to clear my name.”

Speaking to reporters outside the court after the hearing, McBride said he’s argued dozens of bail hearings in federal court and none of them lasted as long as Thursday’s did. “And guess what? We’re still not done yet.”

“The judge has some questions about what will happen if Andrew and Tristan Tate are deprived of their opportunity to go to the Romanian proceedings,” McBride added.

The Tate brothers, who openly describe themselves as misogynists, built a global following by promoting a lavish, hypermasculine lifestyle through their social media empire.

Prosecutors cited years of social media posts in which the Tate brothers bragged about their wealth and having multiple passports, arguing they had the means and intent to evade authorities if released from federal custody. The brothers’ defense lawyers countered that the UK allegations are years old, have not resulted in convictions, and their claims to be wealthy were exaggerated to promote online businesses and to generate attention.

The UK charges include allegations of rape and human trafficking involving a total of seven victims. Andrew Tate faces 42 charges and Tristan Tate 17, according to prosecutors. Among the additional counts against Andrew are allegations of making or distributing indecent images of children and possessing extreme pornography.

Neither Andrew nor Tristan has formally answered the charges in court, but they have repeatedly denied the allegations, with Andrew previously describing himself and his brother as “very innocent men.”

The Tates’defense lawyersargued they were too recognizable to disappear if released on bail, saying the brothers shared their movements almost daily with millions of followers. They also proposed that the brothers surrender their passports, wear GPS monitors, and post bond in an amount set by the court.

But bail is extremely rare in international extradition cases. Detainees face a strong presumption against release and must demonstrate “special circumstances,” while also showing they are neither flight risks nor dangers to the community.

After years of legal proceedings in the United Kingdom and Romania, the Tates were arrested in Miami by US Marshals on July 18 on provisional arrest warrants requested by Britain.

The Tate brothers told the US federal judge on Thursday they were merely playing characters when they said outrageous potentially incriminating “stupid things” online.

“Top G says a lot of outlandish things; people don’t take Top G seriously. It’s just a communication method.” Tristan Tate said on the witness stand, referring to Andrew by his nickname.

Assistant US Attorney Abbie Waxman asked Tristan Tate whether he lies. He responded, “I play a character.”

In at times angry, loud testimony, Andrew claimed being held in a Miami jail was preventing him from speaking to his legal team and attending his ongoing criminal proceedings in Romania and civil cases in the US.

“I’m going to lose just because I can’t participate on a case I …. can beat,” Andrew said.

In the separate case in Romania, the pair are facing charges of human trafficking and forming an organized criminal group to sexuallyexploit women. They have also repeatedly rejected the allegations made against them in that case.

After the brothers testified, prosecutors rejected the claim they are just performing as online characters.

Waxman played a video for the court in which Andrew was shown brandishing a machete, demonstrating what he saw as the basic moves of pimping. “Slap, slap, grab, choke, shut up b*tch, sex,” he says in the clip.

“They promote incredible violence against women,” Waxman said. “It is not a character, it is who they are.”

Prosecutors cited the Tate brothers’ extensive international travel, substantial financial resources and past statements that they characterized as evidence that the brothers could try to evade authorities. They also alleged that the brothers, who are dual US-UK citizens, hold passports from multiple countries that were issued under false names.

In a widely circulated video, Andrew says: “I have seven passports. I have 15 driver’s licenses.” He also brags about having residences in more than 30 countries and says he uses bank accounts in 40. Tate says if police stop him, he can simply “pull out a license from some random country.”

US prosecutors also said the Tates “appear to have the financial means” to evade justice, citing the brothers’ claims to be billionaires and social media posts featuring private jets, luxury cars, cryptocurrency, and a $50 million yacht, for which Andrew and Tristan each posted video tours as recently as July 14.

Defense lawyers downplayed the Tate brothers’ wealth, saying the $2.1 million Aston Martin and $5 million and $7 million Bugatti sports cars featured in their videos were rented, despite the brothers’ claims of ownership. They also said the pair was paid to promote the “superyacht” they had presented online as their own luxury vessel.

Their legal team urged the court to ignore the Tates’ social media posts as “hyperbole and promotion.”

Court documents have previously suggested the Tates’ online empire brought in millions. In a 2024 UK civil tax case, a judge ruled that police could seize nearly £2.7 million ($3.6 million) from seven frozen bank accounts after finding the brothers had evaded tax on more than £21 million ($28 million) in revenue from online businesses.

If the brothers fail in their bail application, they are likely to remain jailed at FDC Miami for as long as the extradition case continues –– a process that could take months or even years.

UK authorities have until September 16 to deliver the formal extradition request to the State Department. No date for an extradition hearing has been set.

Whether the Tates will be sent to Britain to face trial remains unresolved.
